q1_issues.issue: `(Inheritance assistant_secretary_of_energy_for_defense_programs assistant)` exposes a noun/role modifier as a genus; the compound rule exposes a modifier only when it is an adjectival property predicable of the referent.

the office title is fused into one six-word symbol that no licensed compound route builds — the modifier_noun rule would take the last word (`program`) as the genus — and `defense_programs` is left unlemmatized, so `energy` and `defense program` are unreachable.

q2_gaps: a multi-word office/role title containing internal PPs ("assistant secretary of energy for defense programs") — the compound rules cover only modifier+head-noun fusion and the name rules only capitalized proper names

"then-President Ronald Reagan" — an office title with a temporal modifier attached to a name: the title rule keeps a title inside the `Name` string, the appositive rule makes it a tense-wrapped typing atom, and neither route carries the "then-"
notes: The antecedent-less "he" takes the mandated `person` witness, "after retiring" correctly yields `Before` with no connective atom, and the appointment outcome uses the licensed state-result shape (reified state + `Experiencer` + flat copular atom + `Result`).
